title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's manuscript. It is a page of an English typescript, scanned upside down and probably reused as scrap paper: the neighbouring pages carry Grothendieck's French notes on Tannakian categories, positivity cones and Hom(G_m,G)/G on the other side. The text is the opening of Section IV, 'The Brauer group of a ringed space'. This matches the title and terminology of Maurice Auslander, 'The Brauer group of a ringed space', J. Algebra 4 (1966); the cote mentions a letter (1965), and this is probably a preprint of that paper.

The content, in modern terms:
- Setting: (X,O) is a ringed space with O a sheaf of commutative rings. C_1(X,O) is the category of locally separable O-algebras, i.e. sheaves of Azumaya algebras. It is closed under tensor product (Theorem III.5 of the paper).
- C'_1 is the full subcategory of 'trivial' Azumaya algebras: those isomorphic to End_O(M) with M a faithful, locally projective O-module of finite type. It is closed under tensor product (Theorem II.4).
- Brauer equivalence: S_1 ~ S_2 if and only if S_1 ⊗ End(M_1) ≅ S_2 ⊗ End(M_2).
- The equivalence classes form an abelian group B(X,O) under ⊗, with unit {O}. The inverse of {S} is {S^o}, because the sandwich map S ⊗ S^o → End_O(S) is an isomorphism.
- Theorem IV.1 is cut off at the bottom of the page. It presumably continues with a condition, such as 'iff {S} is trivial' or a statement about the converse.

This is the standard Brauer group of Azumaya algebras over a ringed space, the forerunner of Grothendieck's 'Le groupe de Brauer I–III'.
errors: Theorem IV.1 as transcribed ('If S is in C_1 then S is in C'_1') is false as a standalone claim: not every Azumaya algebra is a trivial End(M). The statement is evidently truncated at the page break and must continue on the next typescript page, which is not among the neighbouring scans.

Minor point: the inverse argument implicitly uses that S is locally projective of finite type and central, so that the sandwich map is an isomorphism. This is presumably built into 'locally separable' via Section III.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript of Auslander's published paper 'The Brauer group of a ringed space', not Grothendieck's own mathematics. Its content is standard and well documented.
transcription_corrections: The page image is rotated 180°; it is an English typescript with handwritten script letters, not a Grothendieck manuscript.
In the formula for η the target is written Hom^O(S,S), with O as a superscript, matching the typescript's notation; the tensor products are written ⊗ with O over the symbol.
The last line (Theorem IV.1) is truncated at the page end; the statement continues beyond this page.
